title: Four City-funded charities registered with the State only after the City had paid them

beats.text: May 3, 2021. A City-funded housing fund registers with the State as a charity.

visual.toLab: the fund registers with the Attorney General

beats.text: Ten months earlier, a City fiscal year had closed. What had the Mayor’s office paid it?

visual.toLab: the fund registers with the Attorney General

beats.text: 10 million dollars.

visual.label: paid by the Mayor’s office, fiscal 2020

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding. Late registration can be cured, and all four did register.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: A California charity registers with the Attorney General, and files a report each year.

visual.kicker: How the State sees a charity

beats.text: This file found 4 City-funded charities that registered only after a full year of City payments.

visual.label: City-funded charities that registered only after a full fiscal year of City payments
visual.sub: one of them, Excelsior Action Group, was sent notices to register

beats.text: In those earlier years: 13.6 million dollars.

visual.label: paid in the years before each registered
visual.sub: what they received, not a loss

beats.text: The first lead is the big one. The day the fund registered, the registry wrote to it.

visual.text: missing reports for the years ending 30 June 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2020

beats.text: Four years of reports were missing, back to 2017.

visual.text: missing reports for the years ending 30 June 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2020

beats.text: All four arrived on one day: June 10, 2021.
Since then, the City has paid it 55.9 million dollars.

visual.label: paid by the City to the fund, fiscal 2020 to 2027
visual.sub: $44.4 million of it from the Mayor’s office in fiscal 2025

beats.text: Its first report after registering lists one source of government money, a federal fund.

visual.title: Its report for the year to June 2021
rows: federal Community Development Financial Institutions Fund

beats.text: Not the City, which paid it 40,058 dollars that year.

visual.title: Its report for the year to June 2021
rows: federal Community Development Financial Institutions Fund

beats.text: The second lead: Excelsior Action Group. The registry told it to register in August 2020.
A final notice came that October. It registered in September 2021.
By then the City had paid it 626,555 dollars.

visual.label: paid by the Office of Economic and Workforce Development and the Mayor’s office

beats.text: Two more complete the list. Southeast Consortium for Equitable Partnerships, paid in fiscal 2019.

visual.label: Paid in their first year of City money, before the State had a file

Southeast Consortium for Equitable Partnerships, fiscal 2019

beats.text: And SF New Deal, 2,535,592 dollars.

visual.label: Paid in their first year of City money, before the State had a file
rows: SF New Deal (same organization? unknown), fiscal 2020
Southeast Consortium for Equitable Partnerships, fiscal 2019

beats.text: The records don’t show whether it’s the same organization, or two with one name.

visual.label: Paid in their first year of City money, before the State had a file

Southeast Consortium for Equitable Partnerships, fiscal 2019

beats.text: Why does it matter? When the City’s money arrived, the State had no file on them.

visual.label: The State had no file on them

beats.text: And nothing on file shows that any paying department looked.

visual.label: The State had no file on them

beats.text: A fund set up for one City grant may not have seen itself as a charity.

visual.line: A fund set up to receive one City grant may not have thought of itself as a charity that solicits from the public.

beats.text: Not shown: that any money was misused, or that any grant required registration.

beats.text: What would settle it? The grant agreements, and each department’s checks before it paid.

cards.what: The grant agreements and pre-award checks of the four paying departments
SF New Deal’s registry filings, with its employer number

beats.text: As of November 2026, three are registered and one is delinquent.
No official body has judged any of it.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
